content: Ulipristal acetate, commonly marketed under the brand name Ella, is a medication used by women to prevent pregnancy after unprotected sexual intercourse or contraceptive failure, such as a broken condom. It is most effective when taken as soon as possible after the event. However, its efficacy may be reduced in women with a body mass index (BMI) greater than 30 or those taking certain medications that interact with ulipristal. This medication works primarily by delaying or inhibiting ovulation. It may also alter the endometrium, potentially affecting implantation. It is a selective progesterone receptor modulator with both antagonistic and partial agonistic effects. When taken immediately before ovulation, it can postpone follicular rupture. Ulipristal is metabolized predominantly by the liver enzyme CYP3A4 into an active metabolite, monodemethyl-ulipristal acetate. Its half-life is approximately 32 hours, and it has a peak serum concentration of 176 ng/mL about one hour after administration. Protein binding exceeds 94%. How to Use: Take one tablet orally, with or without food, as directed by your doctor. It is crucial to take it as soon as possible after unprotected intercourse. After taking ulipristal, the timing and flow of your next menstrual period may change. If your period is more than seven days late, consult your doctor immediately. Use a barrier method of contraception, such as condoms or a diaphragm, until your next period. If you plan to use hormonal birth control, wait at least five days after taking ulipristal before starting it, as interactions may reduce the effectiveness of both medications. Continue using a barrier method until your next period. Precautions: Before using ulipristal, inform your doctor if you are allergic to it, to progestins (e.g., levonorgestrel, norethindrone), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate dizziness, so limit their use. This medication must not be used during pregnancy, and breastfeeding is not recommended while using ulipristal due to potential risks to the infant. Side Effects: Common side effects include headache, nausea, abdominal pain, fatigue, dizziness, and painful menstrual periods. Serious allergic reactions are rare. If you experience any severe symptoms, such as difficulty breathing or passing out, seek immediate medical attention. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. Contact your doctor for medical advice if you experience any concerning symptoms. Drug Interactions: Ulipristal interacts with several medications, particularly those that affect the CYP3A4 enzyme. These interactions may either increase or decrease the effectiveness of ulipristal or the co-administered drug. Examples include rifampin, St. John’s Wort, and certain antifungal or antiviral medications. Always inform your doctor and pharmacist about all the medications and supplements you are taking to avoid potential interactions. Storage: Store ulipristal at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Properly discard expired or unused medication as instructed by your pharmacist. Do not flush it down the toilet or pour it into a drain unless directed to do so. Important Notes: This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about ulipristal. It is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information tailored to your specific health needs.
